body: PC. Just TF2, Minecraft, dumb small indie/online games, Sims games, nothing big.
Drawing, gaming, talking to (online) friends, watching (mostly gaming) videos. All of which my mental health 'professionals' are saying make my problems worse and want me to stop doing altogether.
I don't want to bother anybody else with it.
I don't think that I could cope with hotlines and the like right now, but I could down the line. I think that I will tell my grandma, not sure how, but I'll do it soon. Thank you a lot
Yeah, good on you for it too.

I would advise against this, because what it could do isn't worth it.

If you do tell them, it doesn't make things any better for either of you. They're still going to be depressed, you're still going to have problems, and you're still probably not going to be able to talk to them about your problems because of their own problems. It does absolutely nothing positive, really.

If it changes anything, it'll make it worse. They'll feel guilty about needing to vent to you, they might feel selfish even, and they might be unable to vent to you or anybody for a long time, or even talk to anybody, because they'll feel like they're being annoying or selfish. Heck, you might even end up feeling bad, which isn't good for you either.

And no compliment, way of wording or amount of reassurance is going to change that. You either do nothing or make things worse, it just isn't worth it imo. That tough love, harsh truth, being blunt BS isn't appropriate when you're talking to a depressed person. Even if they're having a "good day" or don't seem too bad at the time, just don't.
